Hi Oliver,

Since we finally moved into that fixer-upper with the original hearth, I've been hunting for someone who treats {{1}} with the same respect you do. I found a local studio that avoids modern shortcuts like metal fasteners entirely, opting instead for those interlocking shapes that hold steady for a lifetime. They even give you a digital backstory for the {{2}} they use, so we'd know exactly which hillside our table originally guarded. I'm thinking about that empty spot above the fire; if we make a decision before the autumn leaves drop, we can actually get a better rate on a {{3}}. They also have this thoughtful policy where they'll send us a little care package of wax every year to keep the surface glowing, and they even document the entire {{4}} in a book for us to keep. Since we both care about {{5}}, I love that they offer a credit if we pick materials rescued from old local landmarks rather than using new growth. Let me know if you want to head to the Old Mill District with me this weekend to see their gallery.

Warmly,
Claire
